sections.section_title: Clinical Presentation and the 'Pulmonary Mask' Phenomenon
sections.description: The clinical presentation of this pediatric case exemplifies the deceptive nature of pancreatopleural fistula (PPF), a condition where pancreatic pathology manifests almost exclusively through thoracic symptoms. The patient, a young boy, presented with progressive dyspnea and right-sided chest pain over one week. Physical examination revealed classic signs of significant pleural effusion, including reduced chest expansion on the right, stony dullness to percussion, diminished vocal fremitus, and decreased breath sounds in the right lower zones. His oxygen saturation was critically low at 88%–89% on room air. These findings prompted immediate respiratory intervention, including supplemental oxygen and serial thoracocentesis. sections.description: The development of a pancreatopleural fistula (PPF) represents a distinct failure of containment wherein pancreatic secretions breach the anatomical barriers between the retroperitoneum and the thoracic cavity. In the pediatric patient described, the inciting event was blunt abdominal trauma from a bicycle handle, which caused a rupture of the pancreatic duct or a pseudocyst in the distal body and tail. Unlike adult populations where chronic alcohol-induced pancreatitis is the predominant driver, pediatric PPF arises primarily from traumatic injury or underlying genetic predispositions involving mutations in genes such as *PRSS1* (cationic trypsinogen) and *SPINK1* (serine peptidase inhibitor Kazal type 1). The diagnostic journey in this pediatric case illustrates the critical challenge of "pancreatic masking" as a thoracic emergency. Initially, the clinical presentation of recurrent right-sided pleural effusion, chest pain, and respiratory distress led to a working diagnosis of infectious or neoplastic etiologies common in children. The initial thoracocentesis yielded approximately one liter of dark red fluid, a finding that raised immediate suspicion for malignancy or traumatic hemothorax. sections.section_title: Therapeutic Management Algorithm: From Conservative to Surgical
sections.description: The management of a pancreatopleural fistula (PPF) in the pediatric population requires a stepwise algorithmic approach, moving from conservative medical therapy to invasive endoscopic or surgical interventions. Given the extreme rarity of PPF in children—with fewer than 50 documented cases—standardized international guidelines are absent. Consequently, current practice relies on extrapolating data from adult cohorts and synthesizing outcomes from individual case reports, such as the one presented here. The primary goal of initial management is to minimize pancreatic exocrine stimulation, thereby reducing the volume of pancreatic fluid leaking through the fistulous tract and allowing spontaneous closure of the defect.
